title: feat(tooling): the citation census reads a DECLARED fixture address, per address (objectui#9865)
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectui#9865

## The measurement that decides the card, and it says do not close

`SELF_FILES` carves four files out of the citation census because they carry addresses as fixture data. The reasoning is right; the list is narrower than the reasoning. The card asked for the population before anything is built, so that came first.

**Population** — every FALSE citation (`out-of-range` / `non-substantive` / `drifted`) the census reports under `scripts/`, `scripts/__tests__/`, `scripts/pm/` and `eslint-rules/`, re-derived on `origin/main` at `a0176176a` (the card's own reading was taken at `3ecc369bf`, behind `main`, and is superseded).

**Command** — `node scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs --json --list-all`, all six controls passing, so the run certified itself a reading.

**Decision rule** — read the citing text and ask whether the citing file puts the address in a position where it is DATA rather than a POINTER. DATA when the address is an input to, or an expected output of, that file's own assertion or control (a RuleTester `code:` string, a self-test case, a control body a differ must judge, a fixture map key); when it names a path in a SYNTHETIC fixture tree that exists nowhere in the repo; when it is a quoted transcript of a past run; or when the citing prose declares it must not resolve. POINTER otherwise, including a provenance comment beside a fixture row, because the pointer half really does point.

| bucket | false | address-as-DATA | rotted POINTER | data share |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `scripts` | 49 | 7 | 42 | 14% |
| `scripts/__tests__` | 36 | 16 | 20 | 44% |
| `scripts/pm` | 3 | 3 | 0 | 100% |
| `eslint-rules` | 10 | 5 | 5 | 50% |
| **total** | **98** | **31** | **67** | **31.6%** |

**Positive control, two-sided, on that same run.** The census's own FIRING control — `scripts/check-doc-component-types.mjs:756` citing `ActionRunner.ts:112`, verified rotted by content — lands in POINTER. The card's three attested decoys in `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` land in DATA. A reader that carved out everything would put the first in DATA; one that carved out nothing would put the last three in POINTER. Neither happened.

⇒ 31.6% is not a handful. The headline false count carries a floor of correct-by-construction entries roughly a third the size of the directories a tooling reader actually patrols, so the card stands and deliverable 2 is justified.

## The mechanism — a DECLARED class, per address

Report-only, inside the census's existing posture. ⛔ No new gate, ⛔ no blocking behaviour, ⛔ no new npm script, ⛔ no new CI context, and `SELF_FILES` is byte-identical.

A by-name list over a property that holds of many files is the same drift one level up, and it carves out WHOLE FILES when what is fixture data is ONE ADDRESS inside them. So the citing file declares it, beside the address, as `fixture-address: REASON` within `DECLARATION_WINDOW` lines:

- **The reason is REQUIRED.** A bare marker is a mute button: it drops a row and tells a reader nothing about whether the drop was right. The reason is the only thing an auditor of this carve-out has, so a marker without one does not fire — and that leg is a control in both readers, not just a test.
- **Every declared address is COUNTED AND PRINTED** with its reason and the line that gives it, in text and in `--json` (`declaredRows`, emitted in full whatever `--list-all` says). An unaudited mute button and an audited one differ only in whether the output names what it dropped.
- **The reader carries its own control set**, run on every census through the real `scanFile`: firing on the address's line, firing across the window, refusing beyond it, refusing a reason-less marker, refusing an undeclared address. The declared count is a reading only because those fire, and a failing one makes the whole census refuse — `finalVerdict` now consults them with the rest.
- **One reader for BOTH instruments.** The differential gate differences the declared population through the same `scanFile` (`newCitationsIn({ of: 'declared' })`), so a declaration cannot be read by one reader and not the other. That is the failure the shared `SELF_FILES` already exists to prevent, and it would have come straight back with a second copy.
- **Direction of error is stated, not hidden**: a declaration can silence a genuinely rotted pointer, and the window reaches a neighbouring address. Both are visible in the printed list.

## (a) or (b), and why — (b), and it is live

`scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` carries all three attested instances and is held by open draft objectui#9391, so those three are out of reach this round. I took **(b)**: a declaration point entirely inside the free surface that keys on a declaration rather than a list. Landing the mechanism against fixtures alone would have shipped a live reading of permanent zero, which is indistinguishable from a reader that never fires — the exact failure this census exists to make impossible.

Five live files declare, **none of them named by any list**, all re-measured as held by 0 open pull requests before being touched:

- `scripts/check-changeset-claims.mjs` — the four `BORN_FALSE_CONTROLS` bodies (control input to that gate's own differ)
- `scripts/__tests__/check-changeset-claims.test.ts` — seven fixture strings handed to `lineAddresses`
- `scripts/__tests__/check-i18n-call-site-keys.test.ts` — two expected findings over a synthetic `packages/x/…` tree that exists nowhere
- `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-links.test.ts` — one fixture document body
- `scripts/vite-dts-fail-on-type-errors.ts` — the quoted build-log transcript the file exists to fail on

⛔ These are ANNOTATIONS, ⛔ not repairs: no address moves, no assertion changes, and objectui#8875's reservation of the repair decision is untouched. Live reading: 19 declared, census population 1292 to 1273, false 611 to 594.

Left to a follow-up when objectui#9391 lands: the three instances in `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`, five in `eslint-rules/no-line-address-in-test-name.test.js` (outside this round's declared surface), and six in `scripts/__tests__/check-skill-examples.test.ts` (held by objectui#9584). That is 14 of the 31; the card is not addressed further here for those.

## Ablation — the pin reddens when the declaration is removed

Both legs were run from the committed state, each proved on disk before it was believed, each restored under a `trap` and verified byte-identical against the HEAD blob.

**1 — remove the mechanism.** `const declaration = i >= releasedFrom ? null : declarationNear(lines, i);` replaced by `const declaration = null;`. Anchor occurrences 1 then 0, injected marker 1, blob `c71fccf3` to `f97bbc49`.

```
ABLATED vitest exit: 1 -- Test Files 2 failed (2) | Tests 12 failed | 89 passed (101)
ABLATED census exit: 1 -- 2 of 11 control(s) failed, this run is NOT a reading
The 0 address(es) DECLARED as fixture data
restored blob: c71fccf3... == HEAD blob; git diff HEAD empty
```

**2 — remove the declarations, keep the mechanism.** The four markers deleted from `scripts/check-changeset-claims.mjs`. Occurrences 4 then 0, blob `27feece7` to `29919d26`.

```
ABLATED vitest exit: 1 -- Tests 1 failed | 60 passed (61)
AssertionError: scripts/check-changeset-claims.mjs declares nothing: expected 0 to be greater than 0
declared 19 -> 13, false 594 -> 600
restored blob: 27feece7... == HEAD blob; git diff HEAD empty
```

⚠️ Worth reading carefully: leg 2 leaves the census certifying `11 of 11 control(s) passed`. That is correct and deliberate — the synthetic controls prove the READER works, and a file going silent is a claim about the TREE, which is what the live pin is for. Two different questions, two different instruments.

`type-check:scripts` was shown to reach the edited files rather than assumed to: `tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json --listFiles` names all nine, `.mjs` included via `allowJs`.

**The eslint narrowing is a measurement, not a skip.** ① The receiving population is 5099 files, read from eslint's own config resolution (`ESLint#isPathIgnored` over `git ls-files`), not guessed. ② 9 files linted, counted from `--format json`. ③ `eslint.config.js` declares no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`, so no type-aware rule exists whose verdict on an untouched file could move, and this diff changes no rule, plugin or config file. The repo-wide run remains CI's.

Test and gate figures are from `938766ab3`, the branch head as pushed.

## Corrections to the card, which the filing seat asked for

1. **The 808-vs-809 discrepancy is a real off-by-one in a line-counting instrument, ⛔ not a convention difference.** `wc -l` counts newline terminators (808). The census counts `text.split(LF).length` (809), and the 809th element is the empty string a trailing newline leaves behind — a phantom line that is not in the file. Consequences: the printed `file has N lines` is wrong by one on every trailing-newline file, and a citation to the phantom last line is scored `non-substantive` rather than `out-of-range`. Both verdicts are FALSE, so no count in the card moves. ⛔ Not repaired here: it is a different defect class from this card's, and shifting the boundary moves headline numbers this card is trying to make readable. Filed separately.
2. **"The address is chosen to be unresolvable" overstates the attested decoy.** Re-read with its scope: the comment at `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs:2745-2751` says the TOKEN `path:NNN` must fail the TRACKED-FILE check — `a real path with a line suffix — tracked as a file, NOT as that token, so the suffix form correctly fails`. It says nothing about line 1679 existing. All three sites are self-test fixture strings, and the number is arbitrary: changing 1679 to an in-range line would NOT break the fixture. So the card's "repairing it would destroy the fixture" is not right for these three. The defect is unchanged and arguably worse — there is nothing to repair the address TO, and a reader is invited to try.
3. **The measured class is wider than both the card's and triage's framing.** Triage ruled the shape as making `a deliberately unresolvable address` declarable. Only 3 of the 31 are deliberately unresolvable; the other 28 are simply not pointers — RuleTester inputs, synthetic-tree paths, a quoted transcript. Nothing about them is deliberate, and a mechanism keyed on deliberateness would have missed 90% of the population. Hence `fixture-address` rather than a decoy-shaped name. ⚠️ Whether the quoted-transcript case belongs under that name is a live boundary — one row, declared with a reason that says exactly what it is, flagged here rather than widened in silence.
4. **`SELF_FILES` is the only SELF-exclusion path in both readers — confirmed, with a correction to how it was quoted.** The card's evidence quotes `scannable()` reading `if (SELF_FILES.has(relPath)) return false;`. That function lives in `scripts/check-new-cross-file-line-citations.mjs`, ⛔ not in the census, whose `main()` inlines the same test. A third instrument, `scripts/dollar-dialect-alias-census.mjs`, has its own `scannable()` and its own separate `SELF_FILES` — which is the by-name repetition this card predicted, already present in the tree. The other exclusion paths in both readers are the extension whitelist, `SKIP_FILES`, the 4MB size cap, unreadable files, the released-changelog region and same-file citations; none of them is self-shaped, so the card's reasoning holds.
5. **The fence held and was re-measured.** 18 open pull requests, 1870 filenames (1844 distinct), fully paginated, control `.github/workflows/ci.yml -> [9584]` fired. All four citation-reader files and `package.json` held by 0; `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` held by objectui#9391; `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` held by objectui#9584, so no command-parity row is owed and none is added. The five files annotated above were each held by 0 at that measurement.

## Acceptance notes

- Noted, ⛔ not filed: `scripts/dollar-dialect-alias-census.mjs` duplicates the `SELF_FILES` + `scannable()` shape with its own list. A candidate for the same declaration once this class has settled; nobody is blocked on it today, and the file is not on any queued pull request. Successor: none yet.
- Noted, ⛔ not filed: the `--json` payload now carries `declaredRows` unconditionally while `rows` still honours `--list-all`. Deliberate and documented in place; recorded because it is an asymmetry a later reader may otherwise read as an oversight. Successor: the next editor of this script's reporting block.
